content:
maya: quick heads up — ran a quota simulation for header-driven routing with model-alias pins + fallback to cheaper variants. results look noisy, want a quick sync
omar: can you paste the rule set and the sim summary?
maya: here's a trimmed rule we used:
```
route: /v1/generate
match: header.user_tier == \"growth\" && header.pref_model == \"rwd-3b\"
action: pin_alias: rwd-3b-v2
fallbacks: [rwd-1b, rwd-2b-q4]
quota_scope: tenant_id
```
maya: sim ran 24h of traces from prod traffic sample, ~12k reqs. overall fallback_rate=6.7%, but 1.8% are due to compatibility failures (model not serving the requested feature)
liam: interesting — are compatibility failures from tool-calling/function-calls only? or also seq_len/kv-cache mismatch?
maya: mostly function/tool-calls and structured-output constraints. a few from seq_len overshoot that would have timed out vs cheaper models
eva: do we have telemetry for which condition caused the fallback per request? console currently shows only fallback_rate per route
omar: this is the part we flagged — console UX doesn't expose fallback reasons. we need breakdown: quota-triggered vs compatibility vs capacity. also need per-model alias metrics
liam: +1. for routing precedence question: should an explicit header pin (like pref_model) override a route-level pin? current behavior: route pin wins if compatible, else header pin triggers fallback to header-specified compatible alias. confused state when both exist
maya: yes — edge case: route has pin to a newer major (rwd-4b) but tenant header pins to rwd-3b. when rwd-4b is incompatible with a tool, runtime falls back to rwd-3b but telemetry marks as route fallback, not header match. hard to reason in console
omar: we should emit the decision tree in the trace: e.g., \"matched_route_pin\":true, \"header_pin\":true, \"served_model\":\"rwd-3b-v2\", \"fallback_reason\":\"compatibility\"
liam: that trace shape works. also want a metric that increments on \"pin_mismatch\" when header_pin && route_pin && served_model != route_pin
eva: UX: in rollouts panel show a stacked bar: served-by (route-pin, header-pin, fallback-compat, fallback-capacity). clicking a bucket shows sample IDs + reasons.
imfra-bot: run completed: simulation_id=sim-2140004321-01, reqs=12047, fallbacks_total=807 (6.7%), fallbacks_compat=217, fallbacks_quota=138, fallbacks_capacity=452
maya: infra-bot summary matches. note: capacity-induced fallbacks are due to reserved pool exhaustion for dedicated customers — those show up unevenly across regions
omar: for quota interactions — if quota denies the preferred alias, should we try an auto-quantize step (rwd-3b->rwd-3b-q4) before switching to rwd-2b? that could reduce quality cliff
liam: might be ok as an opt-in policy per tenant. need to surface expected perf/cost delta in console before enabling
eva: UX: in tenant rollout wizard add a toggle: \"Prefer quantized fallback before switching model family\" and show expected latency/cost delta (sim numbers).
maya: implementation notes: runtime needs new outcome labels and emit pinned_source: [route|header|alias|fallback-step] for each decision. also add reason tags [compatibility, quota, capacity, timeout]
omar: we'll need a small schema bump for trace events + update route evaluator unit tests. can we reuse existing rule expr field for a precedence hint? e.g., precedence: [route, header, auto-quantize]
liam: prefer explicit precedence field on routing config. default stays [route, header, fallback] to avoid surprise changes
maya: action items:
- infra: add outcome labels and per-request fallback reason (liam + infra)
- telemetry: new metrics pinned_mismatch, fallback_by_reason, served_by_source (omar + eva)
- console: rollout UX change for quantize-first toggle and stacked breakdown (eva)
- product: write short opt-in doc for quantize-first behavior (maya)
assignments noted, will put a tiny RFC on the thread
deploy-bot: scheduled sim re-run with updated precedence flags: job=sim-rerun-2140004321 at 2024-11-08T02:00:00Z
omar: thanks — will add the trace schema draft to the RFC.
liam: LGTM, will start infra PR next week.
maya: thanks all, sync in #eng-platform-standup tomorrow to confirm progress :thumbsup:
